summary: Adopt a remote-first work policy to expand talent access and reduce overhead.
rationale: Strategic and execution analyses converge on net-positive outcomes. Cost savings from reducing office footprint offset investment in async tooling. Three of five roles voted to proceed.
tradeoffs: Timezone distribution improves hiring range but complicates team scheduling.
Office cost savings are partially offset by home-office stipends and tooling budgets.
risks: Erosion of team culture without intentional in-person rituals.
Legal and tax complexity when hiring across multiple jurisdictions.
Productivity variance for roles that benefit from in-person pairing.
actions: Define and document remote-first norms and async communication protocols.
Audit roles for remote-compatibility and identify any on-site exceptions.
Establish a quarterly all-hands in-person gathering to maintain cohesion.
Engage employment counsel to address cross-region compliance requirements.
minorityReport: The Execution Planner notes that migration timeline estimates are optimistic; a phased 12-month rollout with per-team pilots is recommended before full adoption.

why: Majority of roles support adoption with standard mitigations in place.
Cost modelling shows net-positive ROI within 18 months.
Competitive talent acquisition pressure makes delay costly.
topRisks: Long-term culture drift without structured in-person touchpoints.
topActions: Complete legal compliance audit before first cross-region hire.
executiveDecision.stopGoCriteria: Proceed if legal review completes within 60 days and a culture baseline survey shows >= 70% team readiness.
